APLNG 83: This course introduces the idea of understanding language use as social practice.
APLNG 200: This course is an introduction to the study of language as a communication system and to contemporary thought on the interrelationships among language, culture, and social interaction and their fundamental links to social identities and discourse communities in today's culturally diverse and technology driven environments.
APLNG 210: Having developed since the fifth century in the British Isles, English has now become a global language used by millions of native and non-native speakers around the world.
APLNG 220N: This course will explore how research into language acquisition intersects with the lived experiences of multilingual speakers.
APLNG 230N: This course examines the contribution of language to a variety of social justice agendas by exploring how language is used to form and support unjust social structures.
APLNG 240: This course explores the evolving relationship between language and video games through the lens of applied linguistics.
APLNG 250: This class provides theoretical and practical training to prepare Writing Center Peer Tutors with specific expertise in tutoring international/multilingual students.
APLNG 260N: Applied Linguistics is an interdisciplinary field that investigates and aims to study social issues through a linguistic lens.
APLNG 269: Global Engagement Seminar is a one-credit course for Global Engagement Community (GEC) Living-Learning Community (LLC) residents, and if space permits, non-GEC residents who are interested in cross-cultural engagement.
APLNG 290N: APLNG290N is a critical, exploratory introduction to the discipline of applied linguistics designed primarily for undergraduate students who plan to enroll in the major; as such, the course is a required course for all students who plan to major in Applied Linguistics.
APLNG 297: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
APLNG 310: This is a course on language rights, policy, and planning from individual, group, inter-ethnic, and national perspectives.
APLNG 320N: The course gives students hands-on tools for investigating ideology and propaganda through the analysis of a variety of historical and contemporary texts.
APLNG 402: This course is a linguistic introduction to the relationship between language, culture, and cognition with a focus on Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
APLNG 410: Study and application of principles of North American English phonetics and theories of teaching pronunciation.
APLNG 412: This course provides opportunities for exploring various perspectives on theory, research, and pedagogial applications in second language writing.
APLNG 450: This course is a survey of state-of-the-art research methodologies in applied linguistics.
APLNG 482Y: Application of theories of language to psycholinguistics, philosophy of language, anthropological linguistics, sociolinguistics, bi/multilingualism, second language acquisition and teaching.
APLNG 484: Develop a working knowledge of the structure of English and apply such knowledge to research and/or classroom situations.
APLNG 491: An investigation into current issues in the theoretical bases of second language acquisition.
APLNG 493: Theory, research, and pedagogy that focus on the teaching of English to speakers of other languages in varied contexts.
APLNG 494: This is a required course for all APLNG majors and only APLNG majors may take this course except with special permission from the instructor.
APLNG 496: Creative projects, including research and design, that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
APLNG 497: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
